transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is that... I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. It's like I can’t ever just sit idle. And recently, we got a new work setup at my job, and it's made that a lot harder to hide.

When you're moving from one thing to the next, does it feel like you just can't sit still and need to be doing something, or does it feel more like your mind is racing with worry and you're trying to manage anxious thoughts?

It's not really worry, no. My mind isn't racing with anxious thoughts or anything like that. It's definitely more of a physical need to just be doing something. 

Like, if I have to sit still through a long training video at work, or even just a really slow appointment, I start to feel kind of boxed in. I just get this strong feeling like I need to stand up, stretch, or at least do something with my hands.
How far back does this feeling of needing to move around and do things go? Has it been something you've dealt with since childhood, or did it develop more recently?

It goes back a long way. Yeah, looking back... this was around long before the recent job change. 

I remember back in grade school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. I was always talking out of turn, and they constantly had to remind me to just stay with my work and focus. So, yeah, it's definitely been something I've dealt with since I was a kid.

When you were in school or working on tasks that required focus, did you also struggle to concentrate and keep your attention on what you were doing, or was it mainly just the difficulty sitting still and the urge to move around?

Yeah, it's not just the moving around. I definitely struggle to concentrate, too. Like, at work, if I'm in one of those longer coaching meetings, or if I have to read through a new procedure... I usually start off fine. But after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes kept moving, but I didn't really take in what was said or what I was looking at. So keeping my attention on something is definitely a challenge for me.

Beyond the difficulty concentrating and needing to move around, do you find yourself acting without thinking things through first? For example, do you interrupt people, make impulsive decisions, or do things on impulse that you later regret?

Yeah, I do that. I really don't mean to be rude, but... well, at work, for example. If I hear my coworkers trying to work through a customer problem, I'll just jump right in. I end up giving them an answer before they've even finished talking, or before anyone actually asked for my input. I just kind of blurt it out without thinking first.

Beyond work, have these difficulties with concentration, sitting still, and acting without thinking caused problems in other areas of your life—like in your relationships, at home, or in school when you were younger?

Well, honestly, it's mostly work where I'm really feeling the impact right now. It's actually started showing up in my performance reviews. My supervisors have been pointing out that I leave tickets unfinished, or I make careless mistakes. It's frustrating because I'm trying really hard, and I generally get along great with the customers. But these little errors just end up slowing the whole team down. So, yeah, it's definitely causing some real problems there.

You mentioned work is where you're feeling the biggest impact right now. But thinking back to your relationships or your home life—have these issues with attention, impulsivity, or restlessness ever caused problems there as well?

Honestly, not really. I haven't noticed it causing any major issues at home or in my relationships. Things are pretty relaxed around the house, so I don't have that same pressure to sit still for long stretches or focus on detailed documents like I do at the call center. So, no, I can't really think of any big problems it's caused in my personal life. It really is just work where I'm noticing it.
When you think back to those report cards from grade school where teachers mentioned you were careless and talking out of turn—roughly how old were you when that started happening?

Well, looking back, it was a long time ago. It's been around way before this job change. I was probably in early grade school when it started. I remember my teachers writing on my report cards that I was bright, but that I was careless, talked out of turn, and always had to be reminded to stay with my work. So, yeah, it's been going on since I was a kid.

When you think about those early grade school years when your teachers were writing those comments—do you remember roughly what grade or age you were? Was it around age 6 or 7, or was it later, like around age 10 or 11?

I'd say it was pretty early on, definitely before I was 10 or 11. I remember those comments on my report cards from when I was just starting out in school, so probably around 6 or 7 years old. It's just always been there, way before I ever started working at the call center. The teachers would always write the same kind of things—that I was a smart kid, but I made careless mistakes, wouldn't stop talking when I wasn't supposed to, and always needed them to remind me to actually focus on my assignments.
